title: Aspirin for the Prevention of Ischemic Complications in Giant Cell Arteritis
off: Aspirin for the Prevention of Ischemic-Related Events in Giant Cell Arteritis Pilot (ASPIRE-GCA Pilot)
sponsor: Centre Integre Universitaire de Sante et Services Sociaux du Nord de l'ile de Montreal

officials.a: Vasculitis Clinic, Hopital du Sacre-Coeur de Montreal, University of Montreal

summary:
The ASPIRE-GCA Pilot trial will assess the feasibility of a future randomized controlled trial (RCT) evaluating the efficacy of low-dose ASA in preventing ischemic complications in patients with Giant Cell Arteritis (GCA).

ASPIRE-GCA Pilot builds on extensive preparatory work and the findings from this study will inform key feasibility outcomes, including recruitment rate, study-drug delivery and treatment initiation, medication adherence, participant retention, and completeness of follow-up data.
desc:
ASPIRE-GCA Pilot is a national, multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, decentralized trial conducted in centers of the Canadian Vasculitis Research Network (CanVasc), designed to evaluate the feasibility of conducting the full international RCT.

To examine this objective, 120 eligible patients with newly diagnosed GCA will be randomized at a 1:1 ratio to receive low-dose ASA (80 mg/day) or placebo for 52 weeks, in addition to standard-of-care therapy for GCA. Participants will then be followed for 13 months.

arms.d: Participants will receive low-dose ASA (80 mg orally once daily) for 52 weeks, in addition to standard-of-care therapy for GCA.
Participants will receive a matching low-dose ASA placebo (orally once daily) for 52 weeks, in addition to standard-of-care therapy for GCA.

primary.m: Recruitment rate defined as the number of participants randomized per center-month.
primary.tf: Through study completion, an average of 18 months
